## Question

Methicillin resistance in *Staphylococcus aureus* (MRSA) is caused by the
*mecA* gene, carried on the SCC*mec* cassette [@katayama2000]. Does a
standard short-read pipeline (SPAdes assembly, Prokka annotation, Abricate
screening) recover the reported methicillin phenotype of each isolate from its
genome, and which other acquired resistance genes do the isolates carry?

Every number, table and figure below is computed from the workflow outputs in
`results/tables/` when this report renders (`pixi run report`).

```{python}
#| label: setup
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

TABLES = Path("results/tables")
samples = pd.read_csv("metadata/samples.tsv", sep="\t", keep_default_na=False)
assembly = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "assembly_stats.tsv", sep="\t")
reads = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "read_stats.tsv", sep="\t")
annotation = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "annotation_stats.tsv", sep="\t")
hits = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "amr_hits.tsv", sep="\t", keep_default_na=False)
versions = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "software_versions.tsv", sep="\t")
databases = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "abricate_databases.tsv", sep="\t")

order = list(samples["sample"])
phenotype = dict(zip(samples["sample"], samples["phenotype"]))
n_samples = len(samples)
n_reads_samples = int((samples["fastq_1"] != "").sum())


def show(df):
    """Display a table without the row numbers."""
    return df.style.hide(axis="index").format(precision=2, thousands=",")
```

## Data

`{python} n_samples` isolates (@tbl-samples): `{python} n_reads_samples` with
Illumina MiSeq paired-end reads from the European Nucleotide Archive, and the
complete genome of the epidemic community-acquired MRSA clone USA300_FPR3757
[@diep2006] from NCBI, which enters the pipeline as a ready assembly and
serves as a positive control. The phenotypes are those reported by the
submitters.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-samples
#| tbl-cap: "Isolates, their reported methicillin phenotype and the accession of their data."
show(samples[["sample", "strain", "phenotype", "country", "study", "biosample", "run_or_assembly"]])
```

### Reads

```{python}
#| label: tbl-reads
#| tbl-cap: "Read files (FastQC): number of reads, read length range and GC content."
reads_wide = reads.assign(read=lambda d: "R" + d["read"].astype(str))
show(reads_wide[["sample", "read", "sequences", "length", "gc_percent"]])
```

## Assemblies

```{python}
#| label: tbl-assembly
#| tbl-cap: "Assembly statistics from QUAST (contigs of at least 500 bp)."
show(assembly.set_index("sample").loc[order].reset_index())
```

```{python}
#| label: assembly-numbers
spades = assembly[assembly["source"] == "SPAdes"]
length_min, length_max = spades["total_length"].min() / 1e6, spades["total_length"].max() / 1e6
ref_length = assembly.loc[assembly["source"] == "provided", "total_length"].iloc[0] / 1e6
most_fragmented = spades.loc[spades["contigs"].idxmax()]
```

The SPAdes assemblies are `{python} f"{length_min:.2f}"`–`{python} f"{length_max:.2f}"`
Mb long, close to the `{python} f"{ref_length:.2f}"` Mb of the complete
USA300 genome. They differ in contiguity (@fig-assembly):
`{python} most_fragmented["sample"]` is the most fragmented, with
`{python} int(most_fragmented["contigs"])` contigs and an N50 of
`{python} f"{most_fragmented['n50'] / 1e3:.0f}"` kb.

```{python}
#| label: fig-assembly
#| fig-cap: "Number of contigs (left, log scale) and N50 (right, log scale) of each assembly. The reference genome USA300_FPR3757 is complete (one chromosome and plasmids)."
#| fig-alt: "Two bar charts side by side, one bar per isolate. Left: number of contigs on a log scale; the reference genome has a handful of contigs, the MSSA assembly a few dozen, and the two MRSA assemblies several hundred. Right: N50 on a log scale; the reference genome has an N50 equal to its chromosome length, about 2.9 Mb, the MSSA assembly about 200 kb, and the two MRSA assemblies below about 20 kb."
data = assembly.set_index("sample").loc[order]
colours = ["#b2182b" if phenotype[s] == "MRSA" else "#2166ac" for s in data.index]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.5))
axes[0].bar(data.index, data["contigs"], color=colours)
axes[0].set_ylabel("contigs (≥ 500 bp)")
axes[1].bar(data.index, data["n50"] / 1e3, color=colours)
axes[1].set_ylabel("N50 (kb)")
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=30)
    for label in ax.get_xticklabels():
        label.set_horizontalalignment("right")
axes[0].legend(handles=[plt.Rectangle((0, 0), 1, 1, color="#b2182b"), plt.Rectangle((0, 0), 1, 1, color="#2166ac")],
               labels=["MRSA", "MSSA"], frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-annotation
#| tbl-cap: "Features annotated by Prokka in each assembly."
cols = [c for c in ["sample", "contigs", "bases", "CDS", "rRNA", "tRNA", "tmRNA"] if c in annotation.columns]
show(annotation.set_index("sample").loc[order].reset_index()[cols])
```

## Resistance genes

```{python}
#| label: amr-numbers
ncbi = hits[hits["database"] == "ncbi"]
genes_per_sample = ncbi.groupby("sample")["gene"].apply(set).reindex(order, fill_value=set())
has_meca = {s: "mecA" in genes_per_sample[s] for s in order}
agree = [s for s in order if has_meca[s] == (phenotype[s] == "MRSA")]
n_mrsa = sum(p == "MRSA" for p in phenotype.values())
n_meca_in_mrsa = sum(has_meca[s] for s in order if phenotype[s] == "MRSA")
n_meca_in_mssa = sum(has_meca[s] for s in order if phenotype[s] == "MSSA")
n_genes = ncbi["gene"].nunique()
```

**Main result.** *mecA* was found in `{python} n_meca_in_mrsa` of the
`{python} n_mrsa` MRSA isolates and in `{python} n_meca_in_mssa` of the
`{python} n_samples - n_mrsa` MSSA isolate(s): the genotype agrees with the
reported phenotype for `{python} len(agree)` of `{python} n_samples`
isolates (@tbl-meca). Across all isolates, the NCBI AMRFinder database gives
`{python} n_genes` different resistance genes (@fig-amr).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-meca
#| tbl-cap: "Reported methicillin phenotype and *mecA* found in the genome (NCBI AMRFinder database, at least 80 % identity and 80 % coverage)."
show(pd.DataFrame({
    "sample": order,
    "reported phenotype": [phenotype[s] for s in order],
    "mecA found": ["yes" if has_meca[s] else "no" for s in order],
    "agrees": ["yes" if s in agree else "no" for s in order],
}))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-amr
#| fig-cap: "Acquired resistance genes found by Abricate with the NCBI AMRFinder database (identity and coverage at least 80 %). A filled cell means the gene is present; the label on the right is the antibiotic class."
#| fig-alt: "Grid with one column per isolate and one row per resistance gene, filled cells where the gene is present. mecA is filled for the two Japanese MRSA isolates and for USA300_FPR3757 but not for the Dublin MSSA isolate. The penicillinase operon (blaZ with its regulators blaI and blaR1) is present in the MSSA isolate and in one MRSA isolate. Other genes, such as erm(A), erm(C), tet(K), mupA, ant(9)-Ia and fosB, are present in one or two isolates each."
def short_class(drugs, width=28):
    """'a;b;c' -> 'a, b, …' so the labels stay short."""
    names, label = drugs.split(";"), ""
    for name in names:
        candidate = f"{label}, {name}" if label else name
        if len(candidate) > width:
            return label + ", …"
        label = candidate
    return label


classes = ncbi.groupby("gene")["resistance"].first()
matrix = (ncbi.assign(present=1)
          .pivot_table(index="gene", columns="sample", values="present", aggfunc="max", fill_value=0)
          .reindex(columns=order, fill_value=0))
matrix = matrix.loc[sorted(matrix.index, key=lambda g: (g != "mecA", classes[g], g))]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 0.4 * len(matrix) + 1.5))
ax.imshow(matrix.values, cmap="Greys", vmin=0, vmax=1.4, aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(order)), labels=[f"{s}\n{phenotype[s]}" for s in order], fontsize=8)
ax.xaxis.tick_top()
ax.set_yticks(range(len(matrix)), labels=matrix.index, fontstyle="italic")
ax.set_xticks([x - 0.5 for x in range(1, len(order))], minor=True)
ax.set_yticks([y - 0.5 for y in range(1, len(matrix))], minor=True)
ax.grid(which="minor", color="white", linewidth=2)
ax.tick_params(which="minor", length=0)
right = ax.secondary_yaxis("right")
right.set_yticks(range(len(matrix)), labels=[short_class(classes[g].lower()) for g in matrix.index], fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The ResFinder database finds the same acquired genes (@tbl-resfinder); NCBI
AMRFinder also reports the regulators of the penicillinase operon (*blaI*,
*blaR1*) and *fosB*, which is common in the *S. aureus* chromosome.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-resfinder
#| tbl-cap: "Resistance genes per isolate in the ResFinder and NCBI AMRFinder databases."
summary = (hits[hits["database"].isin(["resfinder", "ncbi"])]
           .groupby(["sample", "database"])["gene"]
           .apply(lambda g: ", ".join(sorted(set(g))))
           .unstack("database")
           .reindex(order)
           .reset_index())
show(summary)
```

### Notes on individual isolates

```{python}
#| label: notes
gram_negative_like = sorted(g for g in ncbi["gene"].unique() if g.startswith("blaTEM"))
carriers = sorted(ncbi.loc[ncbi["gene"].isin(gram_negative_like), "sample"].unique())
vf = hits[hits["database"] == "vfdb"]
pvl = [s for s in order if {"lukF-PV", "lukS-PV"} <= set(vf.loc[vf["sample"] == s, "gene"])]
```

- *bla*TEM genes (`{python} ", ".join(gram_negative_like) or "none"`) are
  typical of Gram-negative bacteria, not of *S. aureus*. Found in:
  `{python} ", ".join(carriers) or "none"`. This may point to contaminating
  DNA in that library; we report it but draw no conclusion from it.
- Panton-Valentine leukocidin (both *lukF-PV* and *lukS-PV* in VFDB), a
  marker of community-acquired MRSA such as USA300 [@diep2006], is found in:
  `{python} ", ".join(pvl) or "none"`.

## Limitations

The phenotypes are those reported in the BioSample records; we did not test
susceptibility. Abricate detects genes by nucleotide similarity only: it
does not detect resistance caused by point mutations, and genes split across
contigs of fragmented assemblies can fall below the coverage threshold.
Four genomes are an example, not a survey.
